subject: Data stewardship: erase acceptance checklist and evidence needed to close DPA redlines
messages:
From: Rachel (Acme Legal) <rachel@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-contact@cloud-integrator.io
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data stewardship: erase acceptance checklist and evidence needed to close DPA redlines

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the redlines you sent last week. Legal has one last ask before we can sign: a concrete acceptance checklist and the types of evidence Redwood will provide to demonstrate completed data erasure for EU-resident customer data (including backups and snapshots).

Specifically we want to see:
- What manifest/logs are produced after an erase run
- How long traceability records are retained and where they are stored
- Proof methodology for backups and cold archives (snapshot ids, timestamps, checksums)
- Who the internal custodian(s) are for onshore erase activities and audit contacts

Can you share a short checklist and an example evidence bundle (redacted is fine) so we can map to our Annex B? Our goal is to avoid an open-ended acceptance criteria in the DPA.

Appreciate a response this week if possible.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Ortega
Counsel, Data & Privacy
Acme Co
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Rachel (Acme Legal) <rachel@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data stewardship: erase acceptance checklist and evidence needed to close DPA redlines

Hi Rachel — thanks for the specificity, very helpful. Attaching a first-pass checklist and our current DPA redline (DPA_redline_v3.docx). High-level answers inline below and in the attached checklist.

Quick summary:
- Manifest/logs: We produce a signed erase manifest per customer erase job (JSON + signature) that includes object IDs, blob ranges, snapshot ids, and a per-object status. The manifest and audit trail are written to the customer tenancy audit bucket (EU region) and retained for 12 months by default.
- Traceability records: Operational traces (job id, operator id, timestamps) are stored in the audit store for 12 months; immutable hashes of manifests are stored for 3 years to support multi-year compliance requests.
- Backups/snapshots: We include snapshot ids and retention windows in the manifest; for cold archives we produce a digest that lists archive object identifiers and the purge sequence number. For final proof we can provide a signed statement and relevant snapshot metadata.
- Custodians & contacts: Operations custodian (Markus Klein) is the primary contact for erase operations; Ihave ccd him. For legal/audit escalations, Laura Bennett is the point for evidence review.

Notes/questions:
- We typically retain manifests 12 months by default; if you need a longer retention of the traceability record for your audit window we can propose an addendum (we flagged 3-year hash storage as a compromise).
- For customers requiring certified erasure of cold archives, we recommend a short operational runbook and a scheduled hands-off verification window; this is heavier operationally and typically requested under enterprise contracts.

Next steps: please review the attached checklist (erase-evidence-checklist-v1.xlsx). If acceptable, we can add a short Annex describing the manifest format and acceptance criteria to the DPA and close redlines.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data stewardship: erase acceptance checklist and evidence needed to close DPA redlines

Thanks Sofia — I reviewed the draft checklist and DPA redline. A couple of suggested clarifications from legal ops/engineering perspective:

1) Manifest retention: change default manifest retention from "12 months" to "12 months, unless Customer requests extended retention in Annex B (up to 36 months)". That ties the retention to contract language rather than product defaults.

2) Backup/snapshot proof: add a required field in the manifest called "archive_purge_ticket" and "archive_digest_checksum"; that makes the acceptance criteria machine-checkable.

3) Escrow/third-party copies: confirm that any third-party provider (e.g., partner mirror) will be included in the manifest or that Redwood will provide a statement of non-applicability if none exist.

4) Evidence delivery: propose two delivery channels — secure S3 share (preferred) or signed PDF bundle via DocuSign link if customer prefers paper trail. Add a sample DocuSign link in the Annex for flow clarity.

Markus, can you confirm the technical feasibility of producing archive_digest_checksum for Glacier-style cold archives? If it requires a separate re-hydration step, we should call that out and provide an estimated window (we should avoid leaving it unspecified in the DPA).

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Rachel (Acme Legal) <rachel@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data stewardship: erase acceptance checklist and evidence needed to close DPA redlines

Rachel/Team — thanks, all. Quick responses and proposed DPA appendix language below.

- Retention linkage: agreed with Laura; we'll phrase as "default product retention is 12 months; Customer may request extended manifest retention up to 36 months in Annex B."
- archive_digest_checksum: Markus confirmed we can generate a digest for cold-archive objects but if re-hydration is required, the evidence window is up to 7 business days (we'll include the exact SLA in the Annex).
- Third-party copies: we'll include a manifest flag "third_party_in_scope": true/false. If false, Redwood will provide a signed non-applicability statement.
- Evidence delivery: support secure S3 share (pre-provisioned, time-limited access) and signed PDF bundle via DocuSign. I'll add example Drive and HubSpot links in the Annex for process flows.

Action items:
- I'll attach a redlined Annex draft to the DPA (see DPA_redline_v3.docx) with the manifest schema included.
- Laura: can you review the Annex language and confirm the extended retention clause phrasing by EOD Thursday?
- Markus: please confirm the 7-business-day re-hydration SLA and whether we should call out any costs for re-hydration evidence runs.
- Rachel: if this approach satisfies Acme, let us know and we'll prepare a final Annex to attach to the DPA for signature.

Thanks — I'll schedule a 30-minute sync if helpful; otherwise we can close via comments.

Best,
Sofia
